source2: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Egypt i. Persians in Egypt in the Achaemenid period', Encyclopaedia Iranica online - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/egypt-i
notes: Cambyses II defeated Psamtik III at Pelusium (525 BCE) and took Memphis; Egypt became an Achaemenid satrapy. Q4: army mutiny made Amasis king in 570 BCE; Apries killed 567 BCE (Britannica, 'Apries').

source1: Francois Vallat, 'Elam i. The history of Elam', Encyclopaedia Iranica online - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/elam-i

notes: Ebarat/Eparti, ninth Shimashki king, founded the sukkalmah line; last Shimashkians overlapped first sukkalmahs (Vallat). Stolper suggests a brief Larsan (Gungunum) interlude at Susa c. 1925 BCE but no sharp dynastic break; sources disagree. Dates approximate.

successor: French Third Republic (Government of National Defence)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'France: The Second Empire, 1852-70', Britannica online - https://www.britannica.com/place/France/The-Second-Empire-1852-70

notes: After Sedan (1 Sept 1870) Paris crowds forced the bloodless 4 September revolution and a republic; Germans besieged but did not hold Paris. Database name/dates (1816-1870) conflate Restoration, July Monarchy, Second Republic and Second Empire.

successor: Geledi Sultanate and Hiraab Imamate (clan successor states)
notes: Late-17th-century revolts by Ajuran subjects and vassals (Hiraab imamate at Mogadishu; ex-Ajuran general Ibrahim Adeer founding Geledi) fragmented the state. No scholarly source could be opened (Wikipedia leads only); Marka's immediate successor unclear.

successor: British Empire (Crown Colony of Sierra Leone)
notes: Financially troubled Sierra Leone Company transferred its colony to the Crown under the 1807 Act, effective 1 January 1808: administrative absorption, no conquest. Q4: Temne attacks and the 1800 Nova Scotian settler rebellion.

source2: Sean Hemingway and Colette Hemingway, 'The Hellenistic Period', Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History, Metropolitan Museum of Art 2007 - https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/haht/hd_haht.htm
notes: After 323 BCE Alexander's generals fought the Diadochi wars and divided the empire; Cassander seized Macedonia (319-317) and murdered Alexander IV (c. 310/309), ending Argead rule. No capital listed; core taken as Macedonia.

notes: Nupe (with Borgu) conquered Oyo and the court went into exile (Borgu, then Igboho) for about 80 years, returning to Oyo-Ile c. 1610. Britannica dates conquest 1550; database 1535. Q3 Y means loss of core.

successor: Poland - Piast Dynasty II (seniorate at Krakow)
notes: Boleslaw III's 1138 testament split Poland into duchies but the eldest son held Krakow as senior duke with general military, foreign and church powers; the seniorate failed only by the early 13th century. Arguably T1a (fragmentation).
